## Materials and Methods

Full details are given in Supplementary Materials and Methods.

**Pipeline and reference panel.** A Nextflow workflow screened each library for papillomavirus reads with Kraken2 against a combined human/HPV database, typed positives against the complete PaVE reference set (`r stats$panel_n` sequences) by STAR alignment, and classified early versus late viral transcripts. Code and configuration are available as stated in the Data Availability Statement.

**Cohort.** Public human RNA-seq runs were discovered through NCBI Entrez and assembled into a case/control design spanning productive controls (warts, condyloma), epidermodysplasia verruciformis, cutaneous neoplasia (cSCC, actinic keratosis), an unselected-skin null, and cell-line, engineered and non-permissive-tissue comparators. Group assignment read curated SRA metadata, with a small override table correcting studies whose submitted metadata is absent or misleading. Of the `r comma(stats$n_submitted)` libraries that entered the screen, `r comma(stats$n_screened)` returned a result (@suppfig-cohort-flow). The remaining `r comma(stats$n_unscreened)` produced no screening output, either because quality filtering at a 36 bp minimum discarded every read of a short-read library or because the download failed, and they are counted in no denominator: a library that was never screened is not a negative observation.

**Whole-library screening.** Every library was screened in full: no step subsamples reads and `fasterq-dump` was run without a spot limit. This matters because reads deposited from a coordinate-sorted alignment emerge from the SRA in reference order, placing unmapped, and therefore viral, reads at the end of the run. Reads reaching the screen were a median `r pp(stats$spot_med)`% of the SRA-reported spot count, and the medians of the individual sample groups, that is productive controls, EV, cSCC and AK, unselected skin, and the cell-line and engineered comparators, spanned `r pp(stats$spot_tier_lo)`% to `r pp(stats$spot_tier_hi)`%, so no group was read less completely than another.

**Calling infection and productivity.** A reference was assigned when coverage breadth was at least 0.10 and mean depth at least 2. Every library, including negatives, was scored as RPM, the depth-normalized burden used throughout. Productive infection required at least three L1 major-capsid reads, and a control-calibrated detection floor was set at the 5th-percentile RPM of non-cell-line productive controls (`r p1(stats$floor_rpm)` RPM).

**Approvals and consent.** <!-- JID requires approvals and consent to be stated in the Methods, not only in the Ethics Statement (Information for Authors, read 2026-11-02), so this paragraph cannot be deleted outright. It is kept to the bare requirement: the approvals-and-consent fact, and the retrieval and preprocessing sentence that JID's reanalysis rule asks for. The legal basis belongs to the Ethics Statement and the source list to the Data Availability Statement; both were restated here until 2026-11-02, when TP pointed out the overlap. --> We collected no new human material and analyzed only anonymous, publicly archived data, so the work required no ethics committee review or participant consent; the Ethics Statement gives the basis. We retrieved libraries from the Sequence Read Archive by accession with `fasterq-dump`, and applied no preprocessing before the quality filtering and screening described above.

**Confounder control and statistics.** Sequencing depth entered every model as log~10~ library size. Library-selection chemistry was recovered from SRA `LibrarySelection` and, where that field is generic, from library-construction protocol text, resolving `r pp(stats$chem_pct)`% of libraries. Integration was read from the E1:E2 transcript ratio and validated against virus-host junctions and an independent graded cervical series. Logistic regressions and Fisher exact tests were fitted in R, with Wilson intervals for proportions and a Bayesian reanalysis under weakly informative priors as a robustness check (@supptbl-bayes, @suppfig-bayes).
